posts.name: Rab
posts.cooked:
Key Takeaways

MCP now has full access to Open Cloud; connected agents can help you manage your game beyond building Studio. This includes setting up developer products and game passes, changing game settings, reading analytics, and importing assets. A new permission system lets you choose what agents can access in each game.

We’re also adding 3 new Skills that teach agents to use Open Cloud, manage permissions, and import assets.

[Update] November 5, 2026

avienn_a:

[Update] Known issue: In a place that hasn’t been saved to Roblox, execute_luau can’t make HTTP requests. Your client can only reach domains on your HTTP allow list, and you can’t add domains until the place is saved. We’re working on a fix.
Until then, save your place with File ⟩ Save to Roblox or File ⟩ Publish to Roblox , then add the domains you need under Connect to the internet ⟩ HTTP domain allow list . Thanks for trying out the feature all

Hi Creators,

Making a game on Roblox isn’t only building it. You also import every asset you need manually, set up monetization, change settings, publish updates, and monitor its analytics to check how it’s doing. Most of that is managed in Creator Hub, away from where you build.

Today, we’re expanding the Studio MCP server beyond creation. Your MCP client can now call all Open Cloud APIs from the same chat where it edits your place. You choose which ones it can use for each game. We’re also releasing three new Skills that help your agent call Open Cloud, manage permissions, and import models from Blender and other 3D tools.

Manage Your Game From Your MCP Client

Your MCP client can now call Open Cloud with the open_cloud_invoke tool. It can only use the permissions you’ve turned on.

Here’s what you can do from the same chat where it edits your place:

  • Set up a store: Create developer products and game passes, with prices and icons, from one prompt.
  • Change game settings: Update game and place settings, publish, or restart servers without opening Creator Hub.
  • Check how an update did: Read your game’s analytics after you publish.
  • Pull in data from your own service: Call an API you allowlist, and use the response in your place.

Permissions Page1664×1248 436 KB

To manage permissions, open Assistant, click … ⟩ Settings, then select the MCP Permissions tab. Or click MCP in the bottom-right corner of Studio, then select the MCP Permissions tab.

Permissions are saved to your account, for each game. Collaborators set their own.

You choose:

  • Open Cloud scopes: Which Roblox APIs the agent can call.
  • Upload folders: Which folders on your computer it can upload from.
  • Save & load data: Whether data store and memory store calls work from execute_luau.
  • Connect to the internet: Whether scripts can make HTTP requests, and to which domains.

Here are the sections you’ll likely use most:

Section What it lets the agent do
Publish & manage assets Upload models and images, and check their status
Look at your game Read game and place settings, version history, and analytics
Edit your game Change game and place settings, publish, and restart servers
Save & load data Read and write data stores and memory stores from Luau
Connect to the internet Make HTTP requests from Luau to domains you allow
Money & monetization Create and edit developer products and game passes

See the full list in our documentation. Our Skills tell agents to ask you before using permissions that involve money, players, secrets, or publishing. They also tell agents not to work around a permission you’ve turned off.

Import Assets From Your Other Tools

Ask the agent to bring a model from Blender, Maya, or any tool that exports asset types such as GLB or FBX into the place you have open. It exports, uploads, and inserts the model, then compares the result against the source and fixes what the import changed:

  • Scale and rotation: Resized to real-world size and turned to match the source.
  • Textures and colours: Dropped textures restored, and grey parts recoloured.
  • Anchoring and placement: Anchored and set on the ground, clear of other objects.

Here’s a sped-up video of Claude Code importing a model from Blender, then fixing its scale and missing textures.

To use it, turn on Publish & manage assets and approve the folder your exports go into. Uploads are permanent and go through moderation like any other asset. Our import Skill tells the agent to confirm with you before uploading. You’re responsible for what’s uploaded to your account, including uploads an agent makes for you.

Skills for Open Cloud, Permissions, and Import

We’ve added three new Skills to teach agents how to use these improvements. As with all Skills, agents connected via MCP will have access to them automatically. We’re adding:

  • rbx-open-cloud-usage: How to call Open Cloud with open_cloud_invoke, find the right endpoint, and handle errors.
  • rbx-permissions: Works out which permissions a task needs, checks which are on, and asks you for only the missing ones.
  • rbx-import-asset: Imports a model from an external 3D tool, then checks and fixes it. It builds on the other two.

You’ll find them in the Skills tab. Open Assistant, click … ⟩ Assistant Settings, then select Skills. To change one to fit your workflow, select it and click Duplicate, then edit your copy. Your copy replaces the original, but won’t get our future updates. For more, see Skills.

Other Improvements

  • MCP status in Studio: When you have a place open, the bottom-right corner of Studio now shows whether the MCP server is ready. You can check at a glance, and click it to open settings.
  • Playtests run in the background: Starting a playtest from your MCP client no longer pulls Studio to the front, so you can keep working while the agent tests.
  • MCP stays on after restart: Fixed a bug where the MCP server setting could turn itself off when you restarted Studio.
  • More reliable connections: Fixed bugs where Studio could show “No clients connected” while a client was connected, or drop off after reconnecting. Each place also gets a new Studio ID when you switch places, so agents don’t target the wrong one.

What’s Next

We’ll keep adding Skills for common workflows in the coming months and continue to roll out MCP features to support your workflows. Let us know which workflow you’d like a Skill for next, and which permissions you’re missing.

Happy creating!

The Roblox Studio Team

FAQs

Click here to view

Do I need an Open Cloud API key?

  • No. Studio handles access for you, limited to the permissions you’ve turned on for that game.

If I work with collaborators, do my permissions apply to them?

  • No. Permissions are saved per person, for each game. Each collaborator chooses their own.

Does this work with the Assistant built into Studio?

  • No. These permissions and Skills apply to external MCP clients only.

Can the agent delete assets it uploads?

  • No. Open Cloud can’t delete or archive models or images. If you want to remove one, use the Creator Dashboard. This is why our import Skill tells the agent to ask before uploading.

My agent says an endpoint refused a permission I’ve already turned on. What happened?

  • Some Open Cloud endpoints accept API keys but not the token Studio uses for MCP. You can’t fix this from your permissions. The agent will use a Studio tool instead, or point you to the Creator Dashboard.

Why can’t my agent write to a data store even with the permission on?

  • Data stores also need Game Settings → Security → Enable Studio Access to API Services. That’s a game setting, separate from your MCP permissions.

Can the agent turn on permissions itself?

  • No. Only you can change your permissions in Studio.

Whose account do imported assets go on?

  • The owner of the game. If a group owns it, uploads go on the group.

posts.name: MasterDaniel
posts.cooked:
This is good, but I really hope Roblox is going to put some systems in place against warnings and bans caused by AIs uploading inappropriate content now.

I uploaded an asset that was made by Claude a couple of months ago and got a warning because Claude had added some fake blood to the texture. Now that agents can do the entire thing over MCP you’re going to end up with devs getting a lot of warnings and potentially bans because of this.

Anything uploaded via the MCP by an agent that then gets moderated shouldn’t result in action against the developer, except in egregious cases where the uploaded asset is blatantly against the rules (no bans for fake blood, but bans for nudity etc)
